attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across the three-node cluster: node1 is the writable primary, node2 and node3 are read-only physical standbys using dedicated replication slots (node2_slot, node3_slot) and a dedicated `replicator` role. node3 required a workaround (its apt path to the internet was hanging) — resolved by copying the .deb packages already cached on node1 to node3 over the cluster's internal network via SSH (host keys were missing on node3's sshd, generated with ssh-keygen -A) and installing locally. Verified writes on the primary propagate to both standbys, and standbys correctly reject writes. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: for each node (standbys node2, node3 first, primary node1 last) captured a boot_id baseline and healthy-service/data proof, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until the node's boot_id changed, and confirmed PostgreSQL and replication fully recovered — including a final post-restart write on node1 that was confirmed present on both node2 and node3.
